variants.title: Searle's apparatus: thermal conductivity of an aluminium bar
variants.sample: Aluminium bar, same size as the copper bar
variants.note: Aluminium conducts less heat than copper, so the tap is set to a smaller flow (0.60 g/s) and the water still warms by about 8 K.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics: thermal conductivity of aluminium 237 W/(m K) at 300 K

variants.title: Searle's apparatus: thermal conductivity of a brass bar
variants.sample: Brass bar, same size as the copper bar
variants.note: Brass conducts about a quarter as well as copper, so the flow is only 0.26 g/s to keep the water rise near 8 K.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics: thermal conductivity of brass (70 Cu - 30 Zn) 109 W/(m K) at 300 K

variants.title: Searle's apparatus: thermal conductivity of an iron bar
variants.sample: Iron bar, same size as the copper bar
variants.note: Iron is a poor conductor for a metal, so the flow is only 0.15 g/s: a faster flow would warm the water by less than a degree.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics: thermal conductivity of iron 80.4 W/(m K) at 300 K
